physically real (9–10 % of the turf normal impulse, load from +0.06…+0.13 s) — about 0.1 s earlier than the reference's +0.25 s

preserved at 5.0 / 5.5 m/s; at 4.5 m/s the knee lands 3.5 cm more lateral and unfolds to 114° by +0.5 s; the folded boot's side / upper now carries 8–11 % (SP2D 1–3 %); toe / sole ≈ 0, studs 0
answers: Can SP2D simply be accelerated? Partly. Compressing SP2D's own schedule (E0–E3) brought "established" from +1.1 s to ≈ +0.5 s but no further: during +0.0…0.3 s the pelvis roll is set by the landing (pelvis on the turf by +0.1 s) and did not respond to a 3–9× pelvis-objective gain or to folded-leg authority 0.35–0.92. Reaching the reference's pace needed the SAME intention started earlier and organised differently: SP2C's tackling-side counter-lean released and the chest opened before contact, then a coordinated trunk lean back / toward the folded side from contact that moves the COM outboard so gravity rolls the pelvis, and a spine settle once lying. The physical slide is not destabilised (never chest-down, no failure, slide within −6…+3 %).
Meaningful load (50 ms mean ≥ 0.10 BW): +0.06 / +0.09 / +0.13 s. Peak 1.1–1.8 BW at the catch (25 ms), 9–10 % of the slide's turf normal impulse.
Established on the folded side / back (trunk ≥ 60°, pelvis roll ≥ 50°, chest not down, held): +0.44 / +0.43 / +0.48 s (SP2D +1.09 / +1.11 / +0.93 s).

Versus the reference's ≈ 0.25–0.30 s: the trunk matches (62–79° at +0.3 s vs 69°); the hand arrives ≈ 0.1 s earlier (the posting arm is already beside the hip at contact); the established side / back posture comes ≈ 0.13–0.18 s later, because the pelvis roll lags the trunk by ≈ 0.2 s.

Does earlier descent reduce the shoulder opening? Yes. With SP2D's own arm targets, earlier descent alone lowered the peak from 152° to 135–145° (E1–E5). The final SP2E commands a slightly LARGER open abduction than SP2D (114° vs 106°) yet peaks lower — the descended torso brings the turf to the hand.
Peak posting-shoulder angle: 134 / 144 / 138°; 121–123° at rest (SP2D 148–154°, 133–142° at rest).
Reference region 130–135°? Approaches it: 4.5 m/s is inside (134°), 5.0 / 5.5 m/s are 3–9° above; the resting arm is below it.

Modest brake? Yes over the slide — 9.1–10.2 % of the friction braking (SP2D 6.5–9.9 %), at the temporary low hand friction; it slides with the body. The catch impulse peaks at 0.28–0.43 BW of braking for ≈ 25 ms.
Chest down? Never (all speeds; chest-up component ≥ 0.83 from +0.3 s). The resting posture is more on the back than SP2D's (chest-up 0.88 vs 0.68–0.75; folded side down 0.42–0.46 vs 0.65–0.73).
Artificially seated / upright? No — 0 s with the trunk < 35° after +0.3 s (SP2D 0.26–0.39 s, SP2C 1.85–2.39 s).
Actively controlled? Yes — no regional failure, no whole-body fallback; regional authority ≥ 0.54 throughout; the descent is a tracked intention (targets / pelvis objective), not released authority.

Folded-leg tuck damaged? Not at 5.0 / 5.5 m/s (knee in pelvis at contact (−0.12, −0.36, 0.26) vs SP2D (−0.11, −0.37, 0.25); sole-down −0.61…−0.63; studs 0; toe / sole ≈ 0). At 4.5 m/s the knee lands 3.5 cm more lateral (−0.15) and unfolds to 114° by +0.5 s (SP2D 153°). Lying on the folded side loads the folded boot's side / upper (8–11 % vs 1–3 %).

New joint-limit excursions? Yes, all brief (≤ 0.3 s), at the landing / catch: posting elbow pronation 2.9–6.4° (≤ 0.05 s), posting shoulder 3.6–4.1° (≤ 0.05 s), neck 1.8–7.5° (≤ 0.04 s), folded knee 1.1–4.2° (≤ 0.28 s), folded ankle 1.5–7.0° (≤ 0.11 s; SP2D 1.5–1.7°), folded hip 2.7–3.6° (≤ 0.3 s), lumbar / thoracic ≤ 2.6° (≤ 0.23 s). No sustained excursion (a sustained thoracic one in an intermediate candidate was removed by the spine settle). At 5.5 m/s the tackling heel now skims the turf just before the folded side lands (no load).

Slide distance: 4.26 / 5.58 / 7.02 m vs SP2D 4.53 / 5.65 / 6.84 m (−6 % / −1 % / +3 %) — not materially changed at identical F37.5; the torso now carries 11–12 % of the turf normal impulse (SP2D 1–2 %).
note: SP2E = SP2D's folded-side / back follow-through, started before contact and organised so gravity does the early fall: SP2C's counter-lean released and the chest opened in the air, a fast coordinated trunk lean back / toward the folded side from contact with the pelvis objective following, the folded-side arm reaching from contact, a spine settle once lying. F37.5 unchanged. Remaining for your eye: the pelvis lags the trunk by ≈ 0.2 s, the hand catches ≈ 0.1 s earlier than the reference, the tackling leg swings up as the pelvis rolls back (≈ +0.7–1.0 s), and the rest posture is more back than side.
